ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, PA and PB are tangent to the circle $O$ at points A and B, respectively. C is a moving point on the major arc AB. If $\angle P = 50^\circ$, then what is the degree measure of $\angle ACB$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Draw $OA, OB$ as shown in the diagram,\\
$\because$ PA and PB are tangent to $\odot O$ respectively\\
$\therefore \angle OAP=\angle OBP=90^\circ$\\
$\therefore \angle AOB=360^\circ-\angle OAP-\angle OBP-\angle P=130^\circ$\\
$\because \overset{\frown}{AB}=\overset{\frown}{AB}$\\
$\therefore \angle ACB=\frac{1}{2}\angle AOB=\boxed{65^\circ}$

method.method_draft: First describe the diagram: a circle with center O has tangent segments PA and PB from an exterior point P on the right, touching the circle at A and B; C is on the left side of the circle on the major arc AB, and chords CA and CB form angle ACB. Use the text value ∠P = 50°. Draw radii OA and OB to the tangent points. Since a radius to a tangent point is perpendicular to the tangent, ∠OAP = 90° and ∠OBP = 90°. In quadrilateral OAPB, compute ∠AOB = 360° - 90° - 90° - 50° = 130°. Because C lies on the major arc AB, angle ACB subtends the minor arc AB, whose central angle is ∠AOB = 130°.
